pr_title: Fix a possible use after free in X509v3_asid_add_id_or_range
pr_body:
And clean up partially created choice objects, which have still the default type = -1 from ASIdentifierChoice_new().

Fixes #22700
pr_comments:
On Sat, Nov 18, 2023 at 07:03:10PM +0000, Bernd Edlinger wrote:
> @bernd-edlinger commented on this pull request.
> 
> 
> 
> >          (*choice)->type = ASIdentifierChoice_asIdsOrRanges;
>      }
>      if ((aor = ASIdOrRange_new()) == NULL)
>          return 0;
> +    if (!sk_ASIdOrRange_reserve((*choice)->u.asIdsOrRanges, 1))
> +        goto err;
> 
> We only want this function to fail safe after a memory allocation error.
> The only reasonable thing that the caller can do in the event
> of an unexpected memory allocation error, is abort whatever is
> going on, and clean up everything.

How does the caller know why the call failed? Allocation error is one
cause. Having an inherit marker is another.

While I essentially agree that you should throw away the object, this
diff still leaves the object in a corrupted state while you could easily
leave it entirely unmodified (and sometimes you now do). I don't
understand how such inconsistencies help anything.

For instance calling X509v3_asid_canonize() can still fail on this object.
This seems very bad form. Why not fix it?

> How does the caller know why the call failed? Allocation error is one
cause. Having an inherit marker is another.

As long as there is only one error code for everything,
the caller has to assume that every error is fatal.
It should be easy to avoid the conflicting inherit marker.
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to the master, 3.2, 3.1, and 3.0 branches. Thank you for your contribution.

issue_context.title: Potential use after free in callers of X509v3_asid_add_id_or_range()
issue_context.body:
The RFC 3779 code is undocumented, not very well designed and thus rather dangerous public OpenSSL API. It's full of traps and bugs. It should at least be warned against if not documented. Fortunately, almost no one uses it, but there is now an attempt at exposing bindings to Rust: https://github.com/sfackler/rust-openssl/pull/2053 .

The only internal caller `v2i_ASIdentifiers()` of `X509v3_asid_ad_id_or_range()` allocates and passes one or two `ASN1_INTEGER`s and frees them on failure.

Towards the end of `X509v3_asid_ad_id_or_range()`, ownership of `min` and `max` is transferred to `aor`:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9e75a0b911ffb2ad99190a72a3d740d100edf61f/crypto/x509/v3_asid.c#L218-L221

Subsequently, `aor` is pushed onto a part of `asid`. If the push fails, `aor` is freed and `min` and `max` with it.

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9e75a0b911ffb2ad99190a72a3d740d100edf61f/crypto/x509/v3_asid.c#L223-L229

Here's the fix I landed earlier today: https://github.com/openbsd/src/commit/9b790dc7bd2fca0d59a0ba1870e0a50f867b36fb .

review_comments: Once you called `ASIdentifierChoice_new()`, you have created an `asid` that will no longer be a valid `ASIdentifier` in many contexts. In particular, its DER encoding will be invalid until you actually attach an ASId or an ASRange.

We only want this function to fail safe after a memory allocation error.
The only reasonable thing that the caller can do in the event
of an unexpected memory allocation error, is abort whatever is
going on, and clean up everything.
The application can expect not to create a memory leak of a crash
due to bugs in the error handling.  I have an error injection test
running that detected this error and many others.

FYI: The reason why I remove this object at this point is that the (*choice)->type == -1 here, and that
is dangerous because this object would bypass the type == ASIdentifierChoice_inherit check above,
and this initialization code, and will likely pass a null pointer to sk_ASIdOrRange_push below,
causing another memory leak.
